summary: Optimization and setup tips for hardware ray tracing: cheaper ray-traced material paths, ray-traced translucency/refraction setup, reflection capture fallback, sky dome exclusion, culling cvars and how to judge denoiser quality.
gotchas: Ray-traced refraction needs Translucency Type = Ray Tracing, Refraction enabled and Max Refraction Rays > 1 in the Post Process Volume
Two-sided materials recommended for ray-traced translucency; single-sided gives less accurate results
Foliage, fences and small-hole geometry and indoor indirect-lit scenes are expensive
Denoiser supports up to four samples per pixel

summary: Reference table of ray tracing and Path Tracer properties on the Post Process Volume (GI/reflection method, RT reflections, RTAO, RT translucency, path tracing), on each light type, on actors and on materials.
gotchas: Path tracer Denoiser toggle does nothing unless a denoiser plugin (Intel Open Image Denoiser by default) is enabled
Material Cast Ray Traced Shadows requires the light to also cast ray traced shadows
Use Project Setting on lights follows Engine > Rendering > Hardware Ray Tracing > Ray Traced Shadows

summary: Explains Sphere and Box Reflection Capture actors: how they capture static cubemaps and reproject them, lightmap mixing, using a specified HDRI cubemap, capture and Sky Light cubemap resolution, visualization view modes and limitations.
keys: Reduce lightmap mixing on smooth surfaces
gotchas: Captures are static at runtime; dynamic objects are not reflected
Static lights should not be used with the Reflection Environment because they put direct light into lightmaps
Cubemap resolution must be a power of 2; high values cost a lot of GPU memory
At most 341 reflection captures active at once; box shape only suits hallways/rectangular rooms

summary: Short reference for the Screen Space Reflections post-process settings: Intensity, Quality and Max Roughness.
gotchas: Quality defaults to 50 for performance; smaller Max Roughness can run faster

summary: Lists Movie Render Queue output formats (image sequences, EXR, WAV, ProRes, Avid DNx, Final Cut Pro XML, Command Line Encoder, Prestreaming Recorder) and how to set up FFmpeg via the Command Line Encoder project settings.
gotchas: Command Line Encoder needs an encoder executable (e.g. FFmpeg) and an accompanying image sequence output; single-pass encoding only
WAV Audio output is experimental; non-Sequencer audio has gaps between shots
Final Cut Pro XML is editor-only, not in shipping builds
ProRes and DNx export no audio; DNx is 8-bit only

summary: Describes the deprecated Sequencer Render Movie Settings window (Capture Movie) for AVI/image-sequence output, custom render passes, filename tokens and capture options.
gotchas: Feature is deprecated
Audio capture is experimental, needs the Audio Mixer and real-time playback or it desyncs

summary: Internals of the HLSLCC library that converts HLSL to GLSL via Mesa IR: pipeline stages, parser (flex/bison), compilation functions and how to extend it with expressions, intrinsics and types.
gotchas: UnrealBuildTool does not detect changes to HLSLCC; touch OpenGLShaders.cpp to force a relink
Lexer/parser changes require regenerating C code with flex and bison

summary: Step-by-step tutorial recreating the LensDistortion plugin as a new plugin 'Foo' with a .usf global shader, C++ shader classes and a Blueprint function library, then driving it from a Blueprint to warp a render target.
gotchas: Shader module LoadingPhase must be PostConfigInit
Shader files need the .usf extension
Code samples are old (2018-era RHI API such as SetRenderTarget/ShouldCache) and may not compile as-is

summary: High-level guide to adding global shaders in plugins: .ush vs .usf files, virtual shader paths (/Engine/, /Plugin/), render-thread rules, FGlobalShader skeleton, debug cvars and troubleshooting include errors.
gotchas: Plugins cannot add a new shading model to the Material Editor
Shader-containing modules need LoadingPhase PostConfigInit or you get 'not found' errors
r.DumpShaderDebugInfo=1 fills the disk quickly
All shaders must include Platform.ush/usf directly or indirectly

summary: How-to for keyframing Animation Blueprint variables from Sequencer: expose an enum variable to cinematics, then add Skeletal Mesh Component and Anim Instance tracks to switch Blend Poses by enum.
gotchas: Only variables with Expose to Cinematics enabled appear on the Anim Instance track

summary: Full guide to Substrate materials: enablement and conversion, Blendable vs Adaptive GBuffer, Slab inputs (Diffuse Albedo, F0, MFP), blend and lighting modes, BSDF/operator/helper nodes, parameter blending, translucency, performance and debug view modes.
gotchas: Substrate is on by default for new projects; existing projects upgrading to 5.7+ stay non-Substrate unless opted in
Converting a material to Substrate is permanent, and Substrate materials render black if Substrate is disabled
Adaptive GBuffer only on SM6 PC/Mac/Linux and current consoles, costs more and forces DBuffer decals
Limitations: incomplete platform testing, Beta Path Tracer support, DX11 and Mac issues; glints need r.Substrate.Glints=1

summary: Programmer notes on reading Substrate material data in shaders: TEMPLATE_USES_SUBSTRATE, binding Substrate global uniforms in global shaders, handling Blendable vs Adaptive GBuffer, slab accessors, lighting functions and key .ush files.
gotchas: SceneTextureLookup only returns the first closure with Adaptive GBuffer
Shader API is subject to change; shaders must handle both GBuffer formats

summary: User guide for the 3ds Max VertexAnimationTools.ms script that bakes static-mesh vertex animation into textures or UVs for playback via material functions.
gotchas: Max 8192 vertices per texture
Does not work with Skeletal Mesh animations
Only tested with 3ds Max 2015; set units to centimeters
Textures must be sampled with nearest-neighbor; 16-bit precision

summary: How to run Build Texture Streaming and use the accuracy view modes (Primitive Distance, Mesh UV Density, Material Texture Scale, Required Texture Resolution) to diagnose blurry or over-streamed textures.
gotchas: Decal and Landscape materials are not supported by the analysis
Material Instances keep stale data if a parent changed but children were not resaved
Textures with the same name in one material share required resolution
Non-UV0/world-position sampling falls back to UV channel 0 with scale 1

summary: Reference table of texture streamer console variables such as pool size, mip bias, boost, drop mips, fully-loading used textures and limiting the pool to VRAM.
gotchas: Disabling r.TextureStreaming loads all mips of every texture, even unused ones
r.Streaming.PoolSize 0 means unlimited
Prefer r.Streaming.FullyLoadUsedTextures over disabling streaming

summary: Explains the STAT STREAMING output (texture/streaming/wanted pools, safety and temporary pools, mip categories, inflight requests) and incremental processing of newly loaded levels.
gotchas: Non-streaming allocation fluctuations larger than the safety pool cause streaming in/out cycles
Incremental level processing only applies to Static mobility components; level becoming visible early can hitch

summary: Conceptual overview of the texture streamer's update cycle, how it computes wanted mip resolution, and its retention and load-order priority rules; links to build and metrics pages.

Reference for the Texture Asset Editor: toolbar preview tools, texture info, LOD/mip, compression, texture (sRGB, filter, tiling, Never Stream), adjustment and compositing settings, the Oodle RDO panel and the per-platform resolved settings panel.
gotchas: Non-power-of-2 textures get NoMipMaps on import and cannot texture stream; top mip must be multiple of 4 for compression
Uncheck sRGB when channels are used as masks
Try Encodings changes are not saved; On-disk Sizes are only estimates
Editing a Final-encoded texture switches it to Fast (non-RDO) encode, which can look different
